name: Form
summary: Shows the error and collects the values. It does not decide what an error is.

a11y.apg: The native <form>. What matters is where the error lands: an external error given by name reaches the CONTROL, which is the focal node — it gets aria-invalid and aria-describedby pointing at the message. Measured on 2026-08-13, the failure mode this avoids is the worst of both worlds: red on screen and valid in the accessibility tree, which is what happens when the message renders next to a control the engine was never told about.
a11y.keyboardNote: Measured in a browser on 29/08/2026 (apps/keyboard-probe + tests/visual/teclado-motor.spec.ts). This ficha comes from the lineage that did not have check 30, so it declared keys with no measurement behind them — the merge of the two lineages on 29/08/2026 is what surfaced it. Confirmed: Enter, which submits from a field inside the form. Tab and Shift+Tab are out of the count on both sides by construction: Tab moves focus anywhere on a page, so it never distinguishes one component from another. What this measurement establishes is that there is no ENGINE keyboard here to measure — the keyboard is the document order, which is the correct answer for this component.

props.name: errors
props.description: Errors you already decided, keyed by the Field's name. AUREA VALIDATES NOTHING: no schema, no rules, no resolver, no field state. Validate wherever it suits you — a schema on the client, a server action, the API's answer — and hand the result over. That is why no form library is a dependency here: marrying one would force every project using Aurea to adopt it, including those that already validate another way.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Fires with the collected values, already gathered from the named controls. The native submit is prevented for you.

props.name: children
props.description: Fields and the submit button. The form only stacks them with breathing room — arranging beyond that is Stack and Grid's job, not a third way of doing layout.

props.name: className
props.description: Added to the <form>. Every other form attribute passes through.
